preconditions.condition: For a fine to be applied at all, an approved policy is live. Without one nothing accrues (BR-2).

postConditions: An approved policy exists as a series of steps, and it is the only thing that produces a fine.
Each unpaid invoice carries the fines its age has earned, added as their own lines rather than folded into the original amount.
Every family charged has been notified and shown the updated challan, so nobody discovers a fine at the bank counter.
Students meeting an approved installment plan carry no fine, since a family paying as agreed is not late.
A fine removed by Accounts or School Admin carries a written reason, and both the fine and its removal remain on the record.
A settled invoice accrues nothing further, so a fine is never added to a bill already paid.
Nothing was fined at a figure somebody typed. Every amount comes from the approved policy.

dataFields.name: Step number
dataFields.validation: The order in which the steps apply. Each step is reached in turn (BR-3).

dataFields.name: Days after due date
dataFields.validation: How many days past the due date this step applies at. Must be greater than the previous step's (BR-4).

dataFields.name: Charge type
dataFields.validation: A flat amount, or a percentage of the outstanding balance.

dataFields.name: Amount
dataFields.requiredWhen: The charge type is Flat amount

dataFields.name: Percentage
dataFields.validation: Greater than zero and not more than 100.
dataFields.requiredWhen: The charge type is Percentage of outstanding

dataFields.name: Cap per invoice
dataFields.validation: The most the fines on one invoice may total. Without it a debt can grow indefinitely (BR-8).

dataFields.name: Effective from
dataFields.validation: The date the policy applies from. It does not fine invoices whose steps were already passed before it (BR-6).

dataFields.name: Applies to
dataFields.validation: Which fee types the policy fines.

dataFields.name: Version
dataFields.validation: Incremented each time an approved policy is changed. Earlier versions are kept.

dataFields.name: Waiver reason
dataFields.validation: Maximum 500 characters. Required to remove a fine (BR-10).
dataFields.example: Bank was closed on the due date owing to a public holiday.

businessRules.rule: A fine is applied automatically. Nobody types a penalty amount, because a fine that varies by who is at the desk is not a policy.
No fine accrues without an approved policy that is live. A policy in draft or awaiting approval fines nobody.
The policy is a series of steps. Each step is reached in turn as the invoice ages, and each adds its own charge on top of the previous one.
Each step applies at more days past the due date than the one before it. Two steps at the same age is a policy nobody can explain.
Accounts cannot approve their own policy. Setting a penalty and agreeing to it are separate acts by separate people.
A policy applies from its effective date. It does not reach back and fine invoices whose steps were passed before it existed.
A fine is added as its own line on the invoice, not folded into the original amount. A family must be able to see what is fee and what is penalty.
Where a cap is set, the fines on one invoice stop at it. Without a cap a small debt grows without limit, which no school intends.
A student meeting an approved installment plan is not fined while the plan is being met. Only a missed installment brings them back within the policy.
A fine may be removed by Accounts or School Admin with a written reason. The fine and its removal both stay on the record, so a waiver granted at a counter is visible afterwards.
On every fine the parent is notified and shown the updated challan, so nobody discovers a penalty at the bank counter.
A settled invoice accrues nothing further. A fine is never added to a bill that has already been paid.
Each fine posts to the late fee income account, separately from fee income, so the school can see how much of its income is penalty.

basicFlow.navigation: Login → Fee → Late fee policy → Build policy
basicFlow.userAction: Sets the policy as a series of steps: after so many days late, add this amount; after a further period, add this further amount.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Checks each step applies later than the one before, and that every charge is above zero.

basicFlow.navigation: Late fee policy → Submit for approval
basicFlow.systemResponse: Sets it to Awaiting approval. Nothing is fined in the meantime.

basicFlow.navigation: Login → Fee → Late fee policy → Approve
basicFlow.userAction: Reviews the steps and approves the policy.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Records the approval and makes the policy live from its effective date.
Checks unpaid invoices against their due dates and applies the next step of the policy as each is reached.
Adds the fine as its own line on the invoice, stops at the cap where one is set, and posts it to the late fee income account.
Notifies the parent and shows them the updated challan, so nobody discovers a fine at the bank counter.

basicFlow.navigation: Login → Fee → Late fees applied → Waive fine
basicFlow.userAction: Removes a fine in an approved case, giving a written reason.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Marks the fine waived, reverses its posting, and keeps both the fine and the waiver on the record.

alternateFlows.condition: The invoice reaches a further step
alternateFlows.behaviour: The next step's charge is added on top of the previous fines, up to the cap where one is set (BR-3, BR-8).

alternateFlows.condition: The student is meeting an approved installment plan
alternateFlows.behaviour: No fine is applied while the plan is being met, since a family paying as agreed is not late (BR-9).

alternateFlows.condition: The student has missed an installment
alternateFlows.behaviour: They come back within the policy and are fined from the missed installment's due date.

alternateFlows.condition: The School Admin does not accept the policy
alternateFlows.navigation: Late fee policy → Return with a reason
alternateFlows.behaviour: It returns to Accounts and nothing is fined in the meantime, since only an approved policy is live (BR-2).

alternateFlows.condition: The policy changes for the coming session
alternateFlows.navigation: Late fee policy → Create new version
alternateFlows.behaviour: A new version is built with its own effective date and goes through the same approval. It does not reach back and fine invoices whose steps were already passed (BR-6).

alternateFlows.condition: A family had a genuine reason for paying late
alternateFlows.behaviour: The fine is waived with a written reason. Both the fine and the waiver stay on the record, so a concession granted at a counter is visible afterwards (BR-10).

exceptions.condition: A step applies at the same age as, or earlier than, the previous one
exceptions.messageShown: Step 2 must apply later than step 1.

exceptions.condition: A step carries a charge of zero or less
exceptions.messageShown: Enter a charge greater than zero.

exceptions.condition: Accounts attempt to approve their own policy
exceptions.messageShown: Only a School Admin can approve a late fee policy.

exceptions.condition: The cap has already been reached on an invoice
exceptions.systemResponse: No further fine is added, and the invoice is left at the cap (BR-8).

exceptions.condition: The invoice was settled between the check and the posting
exceptions.systemResponse: No fine is added. A fine is never added to a bill already paid (BR-12).

exceptions.condition: A fine is waived with no reason
exceptions.messageShown: Give a reason for removing this fine.

exceptions.condition: A waiver is attempted on a fine already paid
exceptions.systemResponse: It is refused. Money received is returned through a refund, not by waiving the charge it settled.
exceptions.messageShown: This fine has been paid. A refund is the route, not a waiver.

exceptions.condition: The ledger posting for a fine fails
exceptions.systemResponse: That fine is rolled back entirely and the invoice is left unchanged. The run continues for every other invoice.

departures.requirement: The daily run is safe to execute more than once in a day. An invoice never receives the same step's fine twice.
The run covers 10,000 unpaid invoices within 5 minutes and posts each fine atomically.

openQuestions.question: What are the school's actual steps — days and amounts?
openQuestions.assumption: Not specified, and the policy cannot go live without them.

openQuestions.question: Is there a cap per invoice, and what is it?
openQuestions.assumption: Not specified. Without one a small debt grows without limit (BR-8).

openQuestions.question: Should Accounts be able to waive a fine alone, or should every waiver need School Admin approval?
openQuestions.assumption: Either may waive, per the feature. A waiver at a counter with no second pair of eyes is a risk.

openQuestions.question: Does the policy apply to every fee type, or only tuition?
openQuestions.assumption: All fee types by default. Not confirmed.

openQuestions.question: Should a percentage-based fine be calculated on the original amount or on the outstanding balance?
openQuestions.assumption: On the outstanding balance. Not confirmed, and the two differ once a part payment is made.

conventionsApplied.name: session-and-authentication
conventionsApplied.rule: Every use case except the login use case assumes an authenticated session. Sign out is available on every screen. An expired or invalid session returns the user to the login screen with the message "Your session has ended. Please sign in again."

conventionsApplied.name: role-based-access
conventionsApplied.rule: Access is enforced server-side on every request, not only by hiding menu items. A request for a record outside the actor's permitted scope returns a 403 and the message "You do not have permission to view this record." A use case states additions and restrictions only.

conventionsApplied.name: branch-scope
conventionsApplied.rule: Every record carries a branch ID. Users see only their own branch unless the use case states otherwise. Super Admin, School Admin and Principal may switch branch from the header.

conventionsApplied.name: academic-session-scope
conventionsApplied.rule: Every academic record carries an academic session ID. Lists default to the current open session.

conventionsApplied.name: list-screens
conventionsApplied.rule: Every list supports search, column sort and page-size selection. Default page size 25; default sort is most recent first. Filters are applied before printing or exporting.

conventionsApplied.name: print-and-pdf
conventionsApplied.rule: Every report and list offers Print and Download as PDF, honouring the filters currently applied. Each output carries the school name, branch, academic session, report title, filter summary, generation timestamp and the name of the user who generated it.

conventionsApplied.name: audit-trail
conventionsApplied.rule: Every create, update, deactivation, approval and reversal writes to the audit log: actor, role, timestamp, record type, record ID, before and after values, and IP address. Audit entries are never editable.

conventionsApplied.name: deletion
conventionsApplied.rule: Records are deactivated, not physically removed. Deactivated records are excluded from lists and lookups but remain in the audit trail and in historical reports. A record referenced by a financial transaction can never be deactivated.

conventionsApplied.name: validation-and-messages
conventionsApplied.rule: Field-level errors appear inline beneath the field on blur and on submit. Errors that block the whole action appear as a banner at the top of the form. Successful actions show a toast. No action succeeds silently.

conventionsApplied.name: money
conventionsApplied.rule: All monetary values are stored as fixed-point decimals in the smallest currency unit, never as floating point. Displayed as PKR with a thousands separator and two decimal places. Rounding is half-up at the line.

conventionsApplied.name: dates-times-numbers
conventionsApplied.rule: Dates display as DD-MM-YYYY; date and time as DD-MM-YYYY HH:mm in 24-hour form. Times are school-local. Phone numbers are stored in the registered mobile format.

conventionsApplied.name: language
conventionsApplied.rule: All user-visible strings come from a resource file. No hard-coded text in any screen.

conventionsApplied.name: concurrency-and-locking
conventionsApplied.rule: Last write wins, except where a use case defines an approval lock. Once a record is approved, posted or issued it becomes read-only and can only be changed through its defined reversal use case.

conventionsApplied.name: screen-states
conventionsApplied.rule: Every list, dashboard tile and report defines four states: loading, empty, error and populated. The empty state names what is missing and links to the action that creates it.

conventionsApplied.name: bulk-actions
conventionsApplied.rule: Any bulk operation reports a per-row result, commits valid rows and lists rejected rows with the reason. A bulk action never fails as a whole because of one bad row.

conventionsApplied.name: notifications
conventionsApplied.rule: All outbound SMS, WhatsApp, email and push messages are sent through the Messaging module, recorded in the sent-message log with per-channel delivery status, and use a named template. Use cases reference the template; they do not embed message text.

conventionsApplied.name: default-performance-and-retention
conventionsApplied.rule: Unless a use case states otherwise: a screen loads within 2 seconds and a save completes within 2 seconds at 200 concurrent users; lists paginate above 100 rows; financial and student records are retained 7 years; audit and message logs 12 months; every screen is usable at a 360 px viewport. Fill the non-functional field only to depart from this.

conventionsApplied.name: default-trigger
conventionsApplied.rule: Unless a use case states otherwise, the trigger is: the user navigates to the screen and initiates the action. Fill the Triggers field only where a scheduled job, an event in another module, or an inbound external call also starts it.
